requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
I found no gap. `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/rust.rs#static[PROFILE]` carries the `{impl}` reference and pulls in `KINDS` and the naming helpers. The generic selector builder in the profile code is reached from `PROFILE`, so it needs no reference of its own.

Obligations and the code that carries them out:
- **Syntactic ancestry segments** such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, `mod[local]/fn[run]`: `KINDS` maps grammar nodes to short kinds and names them with `NameRule::Field("name")`. Outline nesting supplies the ancestry. The tests assert `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, `impl[Thing]/fn[run]` and `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`.
- **No module resolution across files**: `mod_item` is mapped to a name only. `mod external;` becomes `mod[external]` with no file lookup. `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` and `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` assert `mod[external]`.
- **Outline nodes for functions, methods, structs, enums, unions, traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases and extern blocks**: `KINDS` has a rule for each of these.
  - Functions and methods use `function_item` and `function_signature_item`.
  - Macros use `macro_definition`, plus `macro_invocation` in item position.
  - Type aliases use `type_item` and `associated_type`.
  - Extern blocks use `foreign_mod_item`, named by `extern_name`.
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts a selector for every one of these kinds: `fn`, `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait`, `impl`, `mod`, `macro[make]`, `const`, `static`, `type`, `extern[C]`, `extern[Rust]` and `extern-crate`.
- **Impl naming as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`**: `impl_name` joins the `type` field and the optional `trait` field. The tests assert `impl[Thing]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` and `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
- **`use` declarations and other unnamed items are anonymous**: `use_declaration` and item-position `macro_invocation` use `NameRule::Anonymous`.
  - `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` asserts that the two `use` selectors start with `use@` and differ from each other.
  - `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` asserts the `macro@<12 hex>` form, and that macros inside function bodies are not nodes.
- **Selector spelling documented**: `md/reference.md` has a "Rust items" section with examples, the impl naming rule, anonymous items and the statement that modules are never resolved across files. It also has a "Selectors" section and an outline profile table.
- **Duplicate names**: `fn[repeated]#1` and `fn[repeated]#2` are asserted, as is the failure of resolving `fn[repeated]` without a suffix.

All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject and run the profile through `outline(...)`, asserting the resulting selectors. I found no unspecified behavior. `extern` naming by ABI string and the `Rust` default are documented in the profile table.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
